2 · Paste the post copy

House District 9 runs from South Anchorage to Whittier. Its data center debate reaches a proposed lease 26 miles south of Deadhorse.

Independent Rep. Ky Holland wants data centers of 50 to 100 MW. Republican John Boyle, STAK Energy's chief strategy officer, is open to big ones on the North Slope. ADN describes STAK's project as 3 gigawatts, 30 times Holland's top size.

Alaska's own lines sit far lower. On May 16th the Senate passed SB 250's 15 MW line. On May 18th a House committee held it. Fairbanks' borough mayor now proposes a 5 MW permit pause. District 9 votes Tuesday, November 3rd.

A box of about 100 kW is the unit, stacked to every size on record, with maps of District 9 and the Slope lease.

Both candidates say a big customer could spread energy costs among more users. Would you want one on your grid at 100 MW, and at a gigawatt?

#AKleg #AlaskaEnergy #DataCenters

Editor's note

Re-scored after the one craft cycle (round 5, the cap): 8.165 against 7.7, no hard fails. Artwork rose 6.5 to 7.0 (07 and 02 improved, 04 and 06 gained a horizon; 08 still shows sky banding at display scale), still under the 8.5 craft floor with the run at the cap. Before posting: (1) the cover never says 'data center'; (2) slide 07's lease facts ran in No.96 five days ago and the dedupe step did not flag No.96's shared STAK Energy and DNR entities; slide 08's state-capacity comparison echoes No.78 (the HD9 race itself is new); (3) neutrality holds; (4) primary turnout is ADN-only; (5) open the elections.alaska.gov and akleg.gov source links by hand; (6) slide 04's 'Alaska has drawn lines' is generous, as its body says; (7) post by Monday, November 2nd, ahead of the November 3rd vote.
The deck never endorses or ranks either candidate. Each gets one frame of equal weight in his own words, and Boyle's former DNR post appears only as an identifier on slide 2, never on the lease frame. The primary turnout (nearly 44 percent, 16 points above the state average) is attributed to ADN on slide 5 because the Division of Elections primary PDF couldn't be read (503 directly, 401 through a reader). The ADN-only primary split (59.9 to 40.1) is used nowhere. The general election precinct CSV places both candidates in House District 9 and is the file cited. STAK's 3 GW is ADN's figure, since the DNR notice gives no megawatts. Anchorage Press says a gigawatt or more, and ADN's $500 million figure was killed. The caption ships byte for byte.

Aftercare (this is where reach is won)

  • Post before Election Day. Tuesday to Thursday 8 to 11 a.m. Alaska time is normally the strongest slot, but District 9 votes Tuesday, November 3rd, so Monday November 2nd, 8 to 11 a.m. AKT is the best fit. Tuesday morning before 11 a.m. is the last useful slot. Posting cadence is your call.
  • Paste the sources comment within 60 seconds of posting. First click the elections.alaska.gov and akleg.gov links to confirm they open, because both sites blocked or failed automated fetches in this run.
  • Reply to every comment in the first 60 to 90 minutes and point each question to its slide (the unit is slide 3, the 5 MW and 15 MW lines slide 4, Holland slide 6, Boyle and the lease slide 7, the state's capacity slide 8, the ladder slide 9). After 48 hours, note saves and comments for the ledger.
  • Keep replies fair to both candidates. The deck ranks and endorses neither, so answer with what each said in his own words, keep STAK's size as '3 GW as ADN describes it' or 'a gigawatt or more', and don't argue the race or the primary result.
